subject: Prompt set collection & model fit follow-up — BrightRetail
messages:
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Alvarez <sofia@brightretail.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Prompt set collection & model fit follow-up — BrightRetail

Hi Sofia —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we can line up a model-fit eval and prompt set collection: 

Recap:
- BrightRetail’s primary use case: conversational product search + SKU disambiguation for web and in-store kiosks.
- Key constraints: low-latency inference (<150ms p50), strict PII redaction from prompts, and handling many short, noisy user inputs (typos/abbrev).
- Success signals you mentioned: 90% intent-correct classification for top intents, and <5% hallucination on SKU attributes.

Requested next steps from Redwood side:
1) We’ll run model-fit evals on a short prompt set (recommend ~200-500 representative prompts including edge cases).
2) Please share your prompt set (can be redacted) using the attached prompt_template.csv. Include: original prompt, context (if any), expected output, and tags (edge_case, numeric, pii, ambiguous).
3) Flag any prompts with PHI/PII — we’ll provide redaction guidance below and a checklist in the redaction_checklist.pdf.

Recommended models for initial eval (we’ll measure latency/quality tradeoffs):
- redwood-ft-2.7b (quantized) — strong latency/cost balance for short queries
- open-llama-8b-q4 — good middle ground accuracy/cost
- llama2-70b (hosted variant) — higher accuracy baseline for top-end quality comparison

Why we ask for the prompts: our evals compare model outputs to your expected outputs and surface common failure modes (redaction misses, hallucinations, ambiguity). We’ll also run a small set of automated quality regressions to ensure later tuning doesn’t degrade performance.

Attachments: prompt_template.csv (simple CSV with example rows).

Can you confirm: a) who on your team will own gathering prompts? b) timeline — can we get an initial set by Tue 10/20?

I’ll set up a short follow-up (30m) to review the uploaded prompts and walk through the redaction checklist if that works.

Best,
Logan
Logan Wright | Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
—
Redwood Inference | https://www.redwood.com

From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 16 Oct 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Prompt set collection & model fit follow-up — BrightRetail

Thanks Sofia — appreciate the quick turnaround. Answers below and a short template example inline.

Redaction guidance (short):
- If prompts contain PII (names, emails, phone numbers, credit card fragments), please replace with placeholders: [NAME], [EMAIL], [PHONE], [CC_LAST4].
- For any prompt containing customer IDs tied to internal systems, either redact or map to stable synthetic IDs (e.g., CUST_001).
- If you prefer, you can upload prompts as-is to a secured S3 link and we will perform redaction inside your private workspace; however compliance teams often prefer customer-side redaction before sharing.

Expected_output examples:
- Single-turn: Prompt: "Show me red sneakers size 8" — expected_output: "FILTER: category=sneakers; color=red; size=8"
- Multi-turn: Prompt 1: "I need running shoes"
  User follow-up: "I want under $100 and good arch support"
  expected_output: "INTENT: product_search; CONSTRAINTS: budget<100; attribute=arch_support"

Template/columns we’d like (see attached prompt_template.csv):
- prompt_id, prompt_text, context (optional), expected_output, tag_list (comma-separated), severity (low/med/high)

Model recommendations rationale (what we’ll evaluate):
- redwood-ft-2.7b (quantized) — target for low-latency kiosks; expect best p50 latency at lowest cost.
- open-llama-8b-q4 — good accuracy uplift for ambiguous queries with modest cost increase.
- llama2-70b (hosted) — benchmark for best-in-class quality where latency is less constrained (e.g., admin tools).

Quality regression concerns we’ll watch for during tuning:
- Redaction fidelity: we’ll test that placeholder insertion doesn’t change intent detection and that models don’t hallucinate real PII back in outputs.
- Ambiguity handling: ensure model prefers clarification vs. guessing SKU attributes.
- Numeric normalization: prices and sizes should be consistently parsed.

Next steps:
- If you can send 10–15 redacted example prompts today, we’ll validate the CSV schema and run a quick smoke eval.
- I’ll seed a shared Drive folder (link below) and add the redaction_checklist.pdf.

Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-BrightRetail-Prompts

Attaching: prompt_template.csv, redaction_checklist.pdf

Thanks — looking forward to the samples.

Best,
Logan

Evaluation plan suggestions:
- Initial smoke eval: 200 prompts (mix of common + edge cases). Measure intent accuracy, exact-match for structured outputs, and hallucination rate.
- Thresholds to validate: intent_accuracy >= 90% (goal), hallucination_rate <= 5% (goal).
- If model meets thresholds on redwood-ft-2.7b quantized, we’ll recommend a dedicated pilot for kiosks; otherwise we’ll iterate on prompts or try larger variants.

Operational ask:
- Can BrightRetail point us to a product owner who can help label expected_outputs for the first 200 prompts? That labeling step reduces ambiguity in eval scoring.
